**Yarra Valley Regional Rail – Community Update: Track Maintenance Plan 2024-25**

**Issued: 15 July 2024**

Dear Community Member,

Yarra Valley Regional Rail (YVRR) is pleased to provide this update on our Track Maintenance Plan for the 2024-25 financial year. As the network operator for the Healesville and Lilydale lines, we are committed to keeping you informed about scheduled works, service changes, and safety initiatives that may affect your local area.

This update covers the period from late July 2024 through to June 2025, and includes information about upcoming maintenance windows, contact details for our Community Liaison Officer, and important safety reminders for residents living near the rail corridor.

**About Yarra Valley Regional Rail**

Yarra Valley Regional Rail network_operator_name Yarra Valley Regional Rail. Record status: current. We manage the rail network between Lilydale and Healesville, including all station infrastructure, level crossings, and track assets. Our team works year-round to maintain and improve the network, with a focus on safety, reliability, and minimising disruption to passengers and the community.

**2024-25 Maintenance Program Overview**

The Track Maintenance Plan 2024-25 outlines a comprehensive programme of works designed to keep the network operating safely and efficiently. Key activities include:

- **Track resurfacing and ballast renewal** – Replacing worn ballast and resurfacing track sections to maintain proper drainage and support.
- **Sleep replacement** – Replacing timber sleepers with concrete sleepers on high-wear sections between Lilydale and Mount Evelyn.
- **Level crossing upgrades** – Improving surface conditions and warning systems at several crossings along the corridor.
- **Vegetation management** – Clearing vegetation along the rail corridor to improve sightlines and reduce fire risk during the summer months.
- **Bridge and culvert inspections** – Undertaking detailed structural assessments of bridges and culverts, particularly after periods of heavy rainfall.
- **Signalling and communication systems maintenance** – Testing and upgrading signalling equipment at key locations.

These works will be delivered through a series of scheduled maintenance windows, during which sections of the line may be closed to rail traffic. We understand that closures can be inconvenient, and we will work to keep them to a minimum while ensuring the safety of our workforce and the travelling public.

**Committee Membership**

- Nillumbik Shire Council

- Healesville and District Railway Preservation Society
- Lilydale Chamber of Commerce

- YVRR Operations, Engineering, and Communications teams

Membership is reviewed annually. Organisations that wish to nominate a representative for the 2025-26 term should contact the Committee Secretary by **30 November 2024**.

**How Community Input Shapes the Plan**

The maintenance windows listed in our previous update are based on engineering assessments of track condition, but they are also influenced by community feedback. For example, the scheduling of the September vegetation management works to avoid school holiday periods followed requests from families in the Mount Evelyn and Woori Yallock areas. Similarly, the decision to run the November drainage works in the evening rather than during the day came after feedback from traders on the Lilydale to Healesville corridor.

We encourage residents and passengers to continue providing feedback. Each quarter, the Committee will review submissions and consider whether adjustments can be made to upcoming works. Where changes are made, they will be communicated through this community update series and through station notices.

**Feedback Received in July 2024**

Since the publication of the first edition, we have received 47 items of feedback. A summary of the main themes is provided below.

It covers the period from September to December 2024 and provides details on overnight closures, revised timetables and alternative transport arrangements. During overnight closures, replacement buses will operate on the following basis:

- **Full line closures (Lilydale to Healesville):** Buses operate to the normal timetable, stopping at all stations. Additional capacity is provided on peak services where possible.
- **Partial closures (Lilydale to Wandin North or Woori Yallock):** Buses operate between the closure limits, connecting with trains at Lilydale.
- **Reduced timetable services:** Trains operate to a modified timetable, with some evening services cancelled. Replacement buses are provided for cancelled services.

Passengers are advised to allow additional travel time during all closure periods. Replacement bus stops are located at the station forecourt or as indicated by signage at each station. Accessible transport options are available – please contact our Accessibility Line on 1800 123 456 at least 24 hours in advance to arrange assistance.
**Yarra Valley Regional Rail – Community Update: Track Maintenance Plan 2024-25**

**Issue 4 – 14 November 2024**

Welcome to the fourth edition of our community update on the Track Maintenance Plan 2024-25. This edition provides an overview of works completed since the last update, a summary of the recently published Safety Incident Report 2024, and an outline of what is planned for the remainder of November and into December.

**Works Completed – October to Mid-November 2024**

The following maintenance activities have been completed since our last community update:

- **Wednesday 16 October to Friday 18 October 2024** – Overnight track inspections and ultrasonic rail flaw detection between Lilydale and Healesville. No service disruptions were required.
- **Monday 21 October to Thursday 24 October 2024** – Vegetation clearance along the corridor between Mount Evelyn and Woori Yallock. Works were completed ahead of schedule, with all trains operating to normal timetables.
- **Monday 28 October to Thursday 31 October 2024** – Resurfacing and ballast tamping between Lilydale and Mount Evelyn. Buses replaced trains between Lilydale and Wandin North as advertised.
- **Monday 4 November to Thursday 7 November 2024** – Level crossing maintenance at Birmingham Road, Lilydale, and Wray Crescent, Mount Evelyn. Trains operated to a reduced timetable during evening periods.

We thank passengers and local residents for their patience during these works. All scheduled activities were completed within their planned overnight windows, with no carry-over works required.

**Safety Incident Report 2024 – Summary**

On Monday 11 November 2024, Yarra Valley Regional Rail published the Safety Incident Report 2024, covering the period 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024. The report is available on our website and in hard copy at Lilydale, Yarra Glen and Healesville stations.

Key points from the report:

- **Overall safety performance** – The number of reported safety incidents decreased by 12% compared with the previous reporting year.
- **Level crossing incidents** – There were three incidents at level crossings during the reporting period. Two involved vehicles failing to stop at activated crossing signals; one involved a pedestrian. No injuries were sustained in any of these incidents.
- **Track and infrastructure** – Six infrastructure faults were reported, all of which were addressed within required timeframes. The most common fault type related to signal activation issues at level crossings.
- **Workplace safety** – There were four minor workplace injuries, all requiring only first aid treatment. No lost-time injuries were recorded.
- **Community and passenger safety** – There were eleven reported instances of passengers accessing the track corridor at non-designated locations. YVRR continues to work with Victoria Police and local schools to address this issue.

The Safety Incident Report 2024 also records progress against the recommendations of the 2023 report. All six recommendations from the previous report have been implemented, including the installation of additional warning signage at high-risk level crossings and the introduction of a new track corridor access reporting procedure.

A key change in this year's report is the inclusion of a new section on near-miss reporting. During the reporting period, 23 near-miss events were reported by train crew and track workers. Analysis of these events has informed the prioritisation of maintenance works in the 2024-25 programme, particularly in relation to vegetation clearance and drainage improvements.

The Safety Incident Report 2024 is a public document. If you would like a copy, please contact our Community Engagement team on 1800 654 321 or email community@yvrr.com.au.

TrackWorks Australia is the maintenance contractor for the YVRR corridor. The YVRR network operates heritage and tourist services between Lilydale and Yarra Glen, with a branch to Healesville. This section summarises the principal hazards identified for the maintenance window (07/07/2025 to 01/08/2025) and the control measures to be implemented. The risk assessment follows the regulator's taxonomy (as defined in the Safety Management System, SMS-2024-02). Contractors are to note that this summary does not replace the site-specific risk assessments (SWMS) required for each work package.

| RA-05 | Exposure to silica dust during ballast cleaning (WP 3D-02) | High | Water suppression to be used; respiratory protection (P2) to be worn; dust monitoring to be conducted on first day of work | Medium |
| RA-06 | Working at height – bridge works (Maroondah Highway Bridge, Croydon) | High | Scaffolding and edge protection to be inspected by a competent person before use; harnesses to be worn where edge protection not practicable; exclusion zone below work area | Medium |

**6.2 Safety Protocols and Regulatory References**

All work is to be carried out in accordance with the following:

- *Rail Safety National Law (Victoria) 2012* and associated Regulations
- TrackWorks Australia SMS, in particular the sections on:
  - Work on or near the track (SMS-2024-02, Section 4)
  - Isolation of traction and signalling power (SMS-2024-02, Section 7)
  - Protection of persons on track (SMS-2024-02, Section 9)
- Each contractor's own SWMS, which must be reviewed and endorsed by the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor before work commences
- The regulator's taxonomy for incident classification (as set out in SMS-2024-02, Appendix C) is to be used when reporting any safety event, near miss, or hazard observation

Contractors are reminded that a copy of the relevant SWMS must be available at the work site at all times. Any deviation from the approved SWMS must be approved in writing by the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor prior to the work proceeding.
**7. Compliance, Reporting and Regulatory Notification**

**7.1 General Compliance Obligations**

All contractors and subcontractors engaged under this Maintenance Plan are required to comply with the conditions of their contract, the TrackWorks Australia SMS, and all applicable legislation. Compliance is monitored by the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor and the Project Manager, with periodic audits scheduled throughout the maintenance window. Contractors are to note that compliance obligations apply from the date of contract award and continue until final acceptance of the works, including any defect liability period.

Contractors must maintain, and make available on request, the following documentation at their registered office and at the work site:

- Current insurances certificates (public liability, workers compensation, and any other insurance required under the contract)
- Plant and equipment registration and inspection records
- Current SWMS for all tasks being undertaken
- Training records for all personnel, including induction and site-specific training
- Any licences or competencies required for the tasks being performed

The Site Supervisor will conduct a compliance inspection at each work site at least once per week during active works. Deficiencies identified during these inspections will be recorded on a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) and issued to the contractor. The contractor must respond to an NCR within five working days, detailing corrective action taken or proposed. Failure to address an NCR in a timely manner may result in suspension of the affected works.

**7.2 Incident Reporting**

All incidents, near misses, and hazards are to be reported in accordance with the TrackWorks Australia SMS and the Rail Safety National Law (Victoria) 2012. The following reporting hierarchy applies:

- Immediate verbal notification to the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor for all incidents involving injury, significant property damage, or potential for serious harm
- Written report on the TrackWorks Australia Incident Report Form within 24 hours of the incident occurring
- Notifiable occurrences to be reported to the Regulator as required under section 102 of the Rail Safety National Law (Victoria) 2012, with the TrackWorks Australia Safety and Compliance Manager responsible for making such notifications

Contractors are reminded that the regulator's taxonomy for incident classification, as set out in SMS-2024-02 Appendix C, is to be used when reporting any safety event, near miss, or hazard observation. This taxonomy is reproduced in Appendix A of this Plan for ease of reference.

For the avoidance of doubt, the following incidents are to be treated as notifiable occurrences and will be reported by TrackWorks Australia to the Regulator:

- Any incident resulting in death or serious injury
- Any incident involving a train or rolling stock, including collisions, derailments, or near misses
- Any significant damage to railway infrastructure, including track, overhead wiring, or signalling equipment
- Any unintended movement of a train or vehicle onto a section of track where a possession is in force
- Any incident involving the release of a hazardous substance

Contractors are not to contact the Regulator directly in relation to any incident unless directed to do so by the TrackWorks Australia Safety and Compliance Manager. All communication with the Regulator will be coordinated through that office to ensure consistency and completeness of reporting.

**7.3 Hazard and Near Miss Reporting**

In addition to formal incident reporting, contractors are encouraged to report hazards and near misses through the TrackWorks Australia Hazard Observation system. Hazard Observation forms are available from the Site Supervisor or the TrackWorks Australia office at Lilydale. Completed forms may be submitted at any time, and all submissions will be reviewed at the weekly safety meeting.

Dear Community Member,

Yarra Valley Regional Rail (YVRR) is pleased to provide this update on our Track Maintenance Plan for the 2024-25 financial year. As the network operator for the Healesville and Lilydale lines, we are committed to keeping you informed about scheduled works, service changes, and safety initiatives that may affect your local area.

This update covers the period from late July 2024 through to June 2025, and includes information about upcoming maintenance windows, contact details for our Community Liaison Officer, and important safety reminders for residents living near the rail corridor.

**About Yarra Valley Regional Rail**

Yarra Valley Regional Rail network_operator_name Yarra Valley Regional Rail. Record status: current. We manage the rail network between Lilydale and Healesville, including all station infrastructure, level crossings, and track assets. Our team works year-round to maintain and improve the network, with a focus on safety, reliability, and minimising disruption to passengers and the community.

**2024-25 Maintenance Program Overview**

The Track Maintenance Plan 2024-25 outlines a comprehensive programme of works designed to keep the network operating safely and efficiently. Key activities include:

- **Track resurfacing and ballast renewal** – Replacing worn ballast and resurfacing track sections to maintain proper drainage and support.
- **Sleep replacement** – Replacing timber sleepers with concrete sleepers on high-wear sections between Lilydale and Mount Evelyn.
- **Level crossing upgrades** – Improving surface conditions and warning systems at several crossings along the corridor.
- **Vegetation management** – Clearing vegetation along the rail corridor to improve sightlines and reduce fire risk during the summer months.
- **Bridge and culvert inspections** – Undertaking detailed structural assessments of bridges and culverts, particularly after periods of heavy rainfall.
- **Signalling and communication systems maintenance** – Testing and upgrading signalling equipment at key locations.

These works will be delivered through a series of scheduled maintenance windows, during which sections of the line may be closed to rail traffic. We understand that closures can be inconvenient, and we will work to keep them to a minimum while ensuring the safety of our workforce and the travelling public.

The maintenance windows listed in our previous update are based on engineering assessments of track condition, but they are also influenced by community feedback. Similarly, the decision to run the November drainage works in the evening rather than during the day came after feedback from traders on the Lilydale to Healesville corridor.

We encourage residents and passengers to continue providing feedback. Each quarter, the Committee will review submissions and consider whether adjustments can be made to upcoming works. **Safety Incident Report 2024 – Summary**

On Monday 11 November 2024, Yarra Valley Regional Rail published the Safety Incident Report 2024, covering the period 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024. The report is available on our website and in hard copy at Lilydale, Yarra Glen and Healesville stations.

Key points from the report:

- **Overall safety performance** – The number of reported safety incidents decreased by 12% compared with the previous reporting year.
- **Level crossing incidents** – There were three incidents at level crossings during the reporting period. Two involved vehicles failing to stop at activated crossing signals; one involved a pedestrian. No injuries were sustained in any of these incidents.
- **Track and infrastructure** – Six infrastructure faults were reported, all of which were addressed within required timeframes. The most common fault type related to signal activation issues at level crossings.
- **Workplace safety** – There were four minor workplace injuries, all requiring only first aid treatment. No lost-time injuries were recorded.
- **Community and passenger safety** – There were eleven reported instances of passengers accessing the track corridor at non-designated locations. YVRR continues to work with Victoria Police and local schools to address this issue.

The Safety Incident Report 2024 also records progress against the recommendations of the 2023 report. All six recommendations from the previous report have been implemented, including the installation of additional warning signage at high-risk level crossings and the introduction of a new track corridor access reporting procedure.

A key change in this year's report is the inclusion of a new section on near-miss reporting. During the reporting period, 23 near-miss events were reported by train crew and track workers. Analysis of these events has informed the prioritisation of maintenance works in the 2024-25 programme, particularly in relation to vegetation clearance and drainage improvements.

**6. RISK ASSESSMENT – 2024-25 MAINTENANCE WINDOW**

**6.1 Key Hazards and Mitigations**

| Ref. | Hazard | Risk Rating (Inherent) | Control Measures | Risk Rating (Residual) |

| RA-01 | Slips, trips and falls on uneven ballast or during night work | High | Walkways to be maintained; lighting provided to all work sites; mandatory hi-vis footwear; housekeeping inspections at start of each shift | Medium |
| RA-02 | Contact with live track circuits / signalling equipment | High | Isolation permits to be obtained from SignalWorks prior to work on track circuit equipment; test before touch; signage placed at all isolation points | Medium |
| RA-03 | Manual handling injuries during rail replacement (WP 3D-01) | Medium | Mechanical lifting aids to be used where available; two-person lift rule for items over 20 kg; pre-shift stretching programme | Medium |
| RA-04 | Mobile plant interaction with workers (excavators, ballast cleaners) | High | Exclusion zones marked; spotter to be appointed for all reversing operations; plant operator must hold current competency; radio communication protocols to be followed | Medium |
| RA-05 | Exposure to silica dust during ballast cleaning (WP 3D-02) | High | Water suppression to be used; respiratory protection (P2) to be worn; dust monitoring to be conducted on first day of work | Medium |
| RA-06 | Working at height – bridge works (Maroondah Highway Bridge, Croydon) | High | Scaffolding and edge protection to be inspected by a competent person before use; harnesses to be worn where edge protection not practicable; exclusion zone below work area | Medium |
| RA-07 | Fire risk from grinding/cutting operations (rail replacement) | Medium | Hot work permit required; fire extinguishers to be located within 10 m of work area; fire watch to be maintained for 30 minutes after completion of hot work | Medium |
| RA-08 | Unauthorised entry to work sites by public (level crossings, urban areas) | Medium | Site fencing and signage to be erected; security patrols after hours at Canterbury Road and Maroondah Highway sites; all site entry points to be logged | Medium |
| RA-09 | Fatigue – extended night shifts during possession windows | Medium | Shift lengths limited to 10 hours; minimum 10 hour break between shifts; fatigue management plan to be submitted by each contractor prior to commencement | Medium |
| RA-10 | Environmental – hydrocarbon spills from plant and equipment | Medium | Spill kits to be available at all work sites; refuelling to occur only in designated areas; any spill to be reported to the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor immediately | Medium |

**6.2 Safety Protocols and Regulatory References**

All work is to be carried out in accordance with the following:

- *Rail Safety National Law (Victoria) 2012* and associated Regulations
- TrackWorks Australia SMS, in particular the sections on:
  - Work on or near the track (SMS-2024-02, Section 4)
  - Isolation of traction and signalling power (SMS-2024-02, Section 7)
  - Protection of persons on track (SMS-2024-02, Section 9)
- Each contractor's own SWMS, which must be reviewed and endorsed by the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor before work commences
- The regulator's taxonomy for incident classification (as set out in SMS-2024-02, Appendix C) is to be used when reporting any safety event, near miss, or hazard observation

Contractors are reminded that a copy of the relevant SWMS must be available at the work site at all times. Any deviation from the approved SWMS must be approved in writing by the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor prior to the work proceeding.

**7. Compliance, Reporting and Regulatory Notification**

**7.1 General Compliance Obligations**

All contractors and subcontractors engaged under this Maintenance Plan are required to comply with the conditions of their contract, the TrackWorks Australia SMS, and all applicable legislation. Compliance is monitored by the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor and the Project Manager, with periodic audits scheduled throughout the maintenance window. Contractors are to note that compliance obligations apply from the date of contract award and continue until final acceptance of the works, including any defect liability period.

Contractors must maintain, and make available on request, the following documentation at their registered office and at the work site:

- Current insurances certificates (public liability, workers compensation, and any other insurance required under the contract)
- Plant and equipment registration and inspection records
- Current SWMS for all tasks being undertaken
- Training records for all personnel, including induction and site-specific training
- Any licences or competencies required for the tasks being performed

The Site Supervisor will conduct a compliance inspection at each work site at least once per week during active works. Deficiencies identified during these inspections will be recorded on a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) and issued to the contractor. The contractor must respond to an NCR within five working days, detailing corrective action taken or proposed. Failure to address an NCR in a timely manner may result in suspension of the affected works.

**7.2 Incident Reporting**

All incidents, near misses, and hazards are to be reported in accordance with the TrackWorks Australia SMS and the Rail Safety National Law (Victoria) 2012. The following reporting hierarchy applies:

- Immediate verbal notification to the TrackWorks Australia Site Supervisor for all incidents involving injury, significant property damage, or potential for serious harm
- Written report on the TrackWorks Australia Incident Report Form within 24 hours of the incident occurring
- Notifiable occurrences to be reported to the Regulator as required under section 102 of the Rail Safety National Law (Victoria) 2012, with the TrackWorks Australia Safety and Compliance Manager responsible for making such notifications

Contractors are reminded that the regulator's taxonomy for incident classification, as set out in SMS-2024-02 Appendix C, is to be used when reporting any safety event, near miss, or hazard observation. This taxonomy is reproduced in Appendix A of this Plan for ease of reference.

For the avoidance of doubt, the following incidents are to be treated as notifiable occurrences and will be reported by TrackWorks Australia to the Regulator:

- Any incident resulting in death or serious injury
- Any incident involving a train or rolling stock, including collisions, derailments, or near misses
- Any significant damage to railway infrastructure, including track, overhead wiring, or signalling equipment
- Any unintended movement of a train or vehicle onto a section of track where a possession is in force
- Any incident involving the release of a hazardous substance

Contractors are not to contact the Regulator directly in relation to any incident unless directed to do so by the TrackWorks Australia Safety and Compliance Manager. All communication with the Regulator will be coordinated through that office to ensure consistency and completeness of reporting.

**7.3 Hazard and Near Miss Reporting**

In addition to formal incident reporting, contractors are encouraged to report hazards and near misses through the TrackWorks Australia Hazard Observation system. Hazard Observation forms are available from the Site Supervisor or the TrackWorks Australia office at Lilydale. Completed forms may be submitted at any time, and all submissions will be reviewed at the weekly safety meeting.
